archival_memory.research_experience_short: I've been involved in undergraduate research since my sophomore year. It's been an eye-opening experience. I initially didn't consider research, but a professor saw my potential in bridging technical coding with user experience. I took the leap and it turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.lab_description: The lab I'm in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with experts from various backgrounds, such as astronomy, environmental science, and neuroscience. We work with massive datasets, often tens of terabytes in size. My main task is to create front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards. I use advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if dealing with 3D data.
archival_memory.lab_description_short: The lab I'm in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with experts from various backgrounds. We work with massive datasets and my main task is to create interactive dashboards using advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if needed.
archival_memory.first_project: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. They had daily temperature readings from buoys across the Pacific, scattered across different servers. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to zoom into specific regions or timeframes. I co-authored a paper on this system, which was surreal and one of my proudest moments in college.
archival_memory.current_research: My current research has shifted to immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can enhance scientists' understanding of complex data. It's a leap from coding websites to creating interactive, 3D environments where users can explore data in a more intuitive way. The process involves experimentation, integrating VR headsets, and finding efficient ways to stream data into these environments. It's cutting-edge, and it's exciting to forge new paths as there isn't a well-established best practice for VR data visualization yet.
archival_memory.research_life: Research life is often misunderstood as me coding away in a quiet corner, but it's actually a lot of reading. I need to stay up-to-date with academic papers, especially when solving complex problems like rendering volumetric data in VR. I've learned to skim through papers, focusing on the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to determine relevance. Occasionally, I share interesting findings with the lab and we discuss how to incorporate those techniques into our workflow.
archival_memory.interactions_with_grad_students: I interact with a lot of graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first, but it's also inspiring. One PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets and integrating it with our VR platform. The idea is to compress the data so that only the necessary points are loaded at once, improving real-time performance. It's fascinating to see theoretical concepts applied in practice. Some of our best brainstorming sessions happen spontaneously, like in the lab break room, where we discuss how to offload processing to the GPU while sipping coffee.
archival_memory.poster_presentations: I've had the opportunity to present our research at smaller symposiums around campus. It's a great experience to distill complex research into easy-to-understand visuals and talking points. Initially, I was nervous about presenting, but it turned out to be a friendly dialogue. People are genuinely interested in what we're doing. I even met a few folks from local startups who shared interesting perspectives on how VR for data visualization could benefit commercial industries like marketing analytics or architecture. It opened my eyes to the potential for research to transition from academia to real-world applications.
archival_memory.publications: I've been fortunate enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a conference submission for the IEEE Visualization Conference(IEEE VIS). We're conducting a user study comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment. Our hypothesis is that VR immersion helps researchers spot anomalies or trends faster. We've completed a small user trial with 15 participants and are now analyzing the data to determine if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a collaborative effort, with each of us handling specific sections. It's a balancing act, especially with my senior coursework and capstone project.
archival_memory.grad_school_plans: I'm considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master's or PhD. I'm drawn to the idea of contributing to cutting-edge knowledge in areas like data visualization or machine learning. However, I also want to see how these concepts are applied in real product development. My mentor suggested that industry experience can provide a better understanding of relevant problems, making a potential PhD more practical. I'm taking my time to weigh the options.
archival_memory.frustrations_of_research: Research can be frustrating, with weeks spent on approaches that don't pan out or discovering that your idea has already been done and improved upon by others. It can feel like a punch in the gut. However, the key is to adapt, learn from existing work, and find new angles or applications. This is the essence of research – building on the foundation laid by others. The sense of collaboration within our lab and the global research community is truly special.
archival_memory.server_crash: A few months ago, one of our servers crashed, and we lost some vital data. It was a stressful experience, but it taught us the importance of data backups. We set up a better backup system and implemented checks to prevent relying on a single point of failure. It was a bonding experience for the lab, and we learned from it.
archival_memory.connection_with_professors: Research has allowed me to connect with professors on a more personal level. My PI is very approachable and supportive, offering guidance on career direction and academic struggles. She's also helped me with scholarship recommendations, networking opportunities, and attending workshops. I recently attended a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I met experts from around the world debating technical details, proposing new frameworks, and engaging in lively discussions. It was exhilarating to witness the forefront of CS knowledge in real-time.
archival_memory.research_journey: My research journey so far has been a mix of hard work and chaos, but it's also been incredibly rewarding. I love the idea that what I do in the lab could shape how scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive work we're pioneering might one day become standard tools, and I'd be proud to say I was part of it from the beginning. The sense of contributing to something bigger is what motivates me. This experience has changed how I think about computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the perspectives I've gained.
